headline: Google Discloses $94.1B in SpaceX Stock, Marking 6% Stake
summary: Google has revealed its significant investment in Elon Musk's space exploration company, holding a 6% stake valued at $94.1 billion.
details: Google has officially disclosed a substantial $94.1 billion investment in SpaceX, acquiring a 6% stake in Elon Musk's private aerospace company. This revelation highlights a significant financial tie between two of the most influential tech and space entities.

The disclosure, made public through regulatory filings, underscores Google's diversified investment strategy beyond its core internet services. This stake positions Google as a key financial backer in SpaceX's ambitious projects, including Starlink and Starship development.

While Google has previously invested in SpaceX, this latest disclosure puts a concrete valuation on its current holdings. The $94.1 billion figure reflects a substantial portion of SpaceX's overall estimated valuation, which has been steadily rising.

This investment could signal a deeper strategic alignment between Google and SpaceX, potentially impacting future collaborations in satellite internet, cloud services, or other advanced technologies. It also provides a clearer picture of the financial landscape supporting the private space sector.

headline_marked: [[Minecraft system requirements raised]] after 17 years: 16GB RAM and 2020s CPU now recommended
headline: Minecraft system requirements raised after 17 years: 16GB RAM and 2020s CPU now recommended
summary: Microsoft has updated the minimum and recommended specs for Minecraft: Java Edition, advising 16GB of RAM and a newer CPU. This is the first spec bump in 17 years, potentially impacting players on older hardware.
details: Microsoft has officially raised the minimum and recommended system requirements for Minecraft: Java Edition, marking the first such update in 17 years. The company states this is to ensure smooth gameplay both now and in the future, allowing for more advanced features.

The new recommendations include 16GB of RAM and a CPU from the 2020s, such as an Intel Core i3-10100 or AMD Ryzen 3 3100. For graphics, an Nvidia GeForce GTX 950 or AMD Radeon RX 460 is now the minimum, with an RTX 2060 or RX 5600 XT recommended.

While the new minimums are considered reasonable for current hardware, players on older systems that previously met the specs might be negatively impacted. These users could consider switching to the Bedrock Edition, though this may mean forgoing some favorite mods.

Microsoft clarified that Java Edition might still launch on hardware below the new minimums, but performance and visual quality are not guaranteed. The company also hinted at a future transition from OpenGL to Vulkan, which could further limit support for older hardware.

Upgrading to meet the new requirements doesn't necessarily mean a costly new PC. Players can find used gaming laptops or desktops for around $350 to $500, potentially securing another decade of smooth Minecraft gameplay if the spec upgrade cadence remains similar.
